title: Flat embedded integral scalar map and its first kernel ideals
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite intermediate field E of PadicAlgCl ell, an element pi of its embedded integers generating the maximal ideal, and a Noetherian scheme X in universe u. Use the actual embedded coefficient maps of [def-sfb-embedded-integral-model-coefficients], transported to the coefficient-sized small site by smallMap. Let phi be the constant-to-continuous scalar map, q the first constant residue map, qB the first completed residue map, and I = kernelIdeal(q), using [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-ideal]. Then I.module is finite type; the completed ring restricted along phi is flat; I.IsQuotientIso(phi) holds; and I.extension(phi) = kernelIdeal(qB) as ideal subsheaves. These are assertions solely about the given ring sheaves and their ideals, with no derived objects or equivalences.

source.place: Paragraph (1); Stacks proetale.tex, section-derived-completion-noetherian (099L); sites-modules.tex, lemma-completion-flat; algebraization.tex, lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence (099I). Finite-type kernel uses the local single generator pi; flatness and canonical quotient are Stacks Tag 093M.

proof.text: Take scalar flatness from the embedded scalar-flat specialization. Obtain the common residue isomorphism, commuting square, local surjectivity and the two principal section kernels from the embedded residue-section presentation.

The named kernel ideal has precisely the sectionwise ring-map kernels. Apply the proved finite-generator ideal helper with the single global section. Ideal.map_span shows that the completed kernel is the ideal generated by scalar images of the constant kernel. The proved local-saturation helper identifies its extension.

For quotient injectivity, apply the commuting square and cancel the residue isomorphism sectionwise. For local surjectivity, apply local surjectivity of q to the inverse residue image of qB(b); its image sieve is covering. A lift a there has b-phi(a) in the completed kernel by naturality and the square. Rewrite the completed kernel as the extension just proved. Combine with flatness.

lean.statement:
theorem integralModelsEmbeddedCoefficientKernels
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ)
    (π : PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1)
    (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1))
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] :
    let φ := IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X (IntegralModelsEmbedded.scalarMap ℓ E X)
    let q := IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X (IntegralModelsEmbedded.residueMap ℓ E π X)
    let qB := IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X
      (completedCoefficientMap X (completedReduction ℓ E π 0)).hom
    let I := ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal q
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} I.module ∧
      SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u + 1}
        ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u + 1}
          ((sheafCompose (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u} X)
            (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).map φ)).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit (siteModuleRings _))) ∧
      I.IsQuotientIso φ ∧ I.extension φ = ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal qB
